details.description: Gladia's asynchronous (batch) speech-to-text API for pre-recorded audio and video, such as call recordings, meetings and podcasts. A file is uploaded and Gladia returns a full transcript, with optional speaker diarization, translation, summarization and other audio-intelligence add-ons in the same call. By default it runs on Gladia's Solaria-1 model, which covers 100+ languages with mid-sentence code-switching; the higher-accuracy Solaria-3 model can be selected instead but is restricted to English, French, German, Spanish and Italian, one language per request.
advantages: Supports 100+ languages with automatic mid-sentence code-switching using the default Solaria-1 model.
Offers an optional Solaria-3 model that Gladia positions as its highest-accuracy option for English, French, German, Spanish and Italian audio.
Gladia reports a 33.9% word error rate on the Switchboard conversational benchmark, which it states is the lowest among the providers it tested.
Built-in speaker diarization lets a caller fix the exact speaker count or set a minimum/maximum via diarization_config.
Bundles audio-intelligence add-ons (translation, summarization, named entity recognition, sentiment analysis, PII redaction, custom vocabulary) in the same request.
disadvantages: Processes only pre-recorded files uploaded by URL; it is not a live/streaming transcription mode.
The higher-accuracy Solaria-3 model accepts only one language per request, with no code-switching, and covers just five languages.
use_cases: Contact-center quality assurance and compliance review

sources.title: Pre-recorded transcription API reference - Gladia docs

notes: The catalog id 'async' names Gladia's asynchronous/pre-recorded transcription product, not a specific Gladia 'model' value (the API's own model field takes solaria-1/solaria-3/solaria-fusion, defaulting to solaria-1). No maker-published benchmark met the higher-is-better 0-100 rule, so evaluations is empty; the 33.9% figure is a word error rate (lower is better) and is placed in advantages instead. Language count is only ever given as '100+', not a named list, so languages is empty.
